title: Sierra Leone Independence
description: Sierra Leone gained independence from Britain on 27 April 1961, with Sir Milton Margai of the Sierra Leone People's Party (SLPP) becoming the first prime minister. The country joined the Commonwealth and the United Nations the same year.

title: First Post-Independence General Elections
description: Sierra Leone held its first post-independence general elections in May 1962, returning the SLPP to power under Sir Milton Margai. The elections established a competitive multi-party system, though regional and ethnic loyalties shaped voting patterns.

title: Sir Albert Margai Becomes Prime Minister
description: Following the death of Sir Milton Margai, his brother Sir Albert Margai succeeded him as prime minister in 1964. Albert Margai pursued more centralising and ethnically divisive policies, increasing tensions between the Mende-dominated SLPP and the northern-based All People's Congress (APC).

title: APC Election Victory Blocked by Military
description: In March 1967, Siaka Stevens of the All People's Congress narrowly won general elections, but was immediately prevented from being sworn in when Brigadier David Lansana, loyal to outgoing PM Albert Margai, declared martial law. A National Reformation Council (NRC) junta took power, suspending the constitution.

title: Counter-Coup Restores Siaka Stevens
description: In April 1968 a group of non-commissioned officers calling themselves the Anti-Corruption Revolutionary Movement staged a counter-coup, ousted the NRC, and handed power to the elected prime minister Siaka Stevens. The episode is often described as a 'sergeants' coup' that used a general strike as leverage.

title: Sierra Leone Declared a Republic
description: On 19 April 1971 Sierra Leone became a republic with Siaka Stevens as its first executive president, replacing the constitutional monarchy. The change concentrated executive power and removed the British monarch as head of state.

title: Boycotted Elections Entrench APC Power
description: The 1973 general elections were boycotted by the main opposition SLPP amid widespread intimidation and violence, allowing the APC to win almost all parliamentary seats. The elections accelerated Sierra Leone's drift toward single-party rule.

title: ECOWAS Founding Membership
description: Sierra Leone was among the sixteen founding members of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) established by the Lagos Treaty in May 1975. The bloc was designed to promote regional economic integration and later became important for security responses to the Sierra Leonean civil war.

title: One-Party State Constitution
description: A new constitution enacted in 1978 made the APC the sole legal party, formally entrenching Siaka Stevens's one-party state. Political pluralism was abolished and the constitution concentrated authority in the presidency, marking the culmination of Stevens's authoritarian consolidation.

title: OAU Summit in Freetown
description: Sierra Leone hosted the Organisation of African Unity summit in Freetown in 1980, a prestige coup for the Stevens government. The extravagant expenditure associated with the summit placed severe strain on the national treasury and contributed to economic deterioration.

title: Momoh Succeeds Stevens
description: Major-General Joseph Saidu Momoh was elected the sole APC candidate and succeeded Siaka Stevens as president in 1985. Momoh inherited a severely weakened economy and a state apparatus hollowed out by corruption, but continued single-party rule.

title: Economic Emergency Declared
description: President Momoh declared a national economic emergency in 1987 as Sierra Leone faced fiscal collapse, depleted foreign exchange reserves, and widespread smuggling of diamonds. Austerity measures and IMF-backed structural adjustment were introduced, deepening hardship for ordinary citizens.

title: RUF Civil War Begins
description: On 23 March 1991, Foday Sankoh's Revolutionary United Front (RUF), backed by Liberian warlord Charles Taylor, launched an armed incursion from Liberia into the Kailahun District. The invasion marked the start of a brutal eleven-year civil war characterised by mass atrocities, amputation campaigns, and the use of child soldiers.

title: Multi-Party Constitution Adopted
description: Under pressure from civil society and donors, President Momoh promulgated a new constitution in 1991 restoring multi-party democracy and term limits. The reform came too late to stabilise the country as the RUF insurgency was already spreading.

title: NPRC Coup — Strasser Takes Power
description: On 29 April 1992, a group of junior military officers led by 25-year-old Captain Valentine Strasser overthrew President Momoh and established the National Provisional Ruling Council (NPRC). The coup was initially welcomed amid frustration at the government's failure to prosecute the war against the RUF.

title: ECOMOG Deploys to Sierra Leone
description: ECOWAS Monitoring Group (ECOMOG) forces, already engaged in Liberia, extended their presence to Sierra Leone from 1993 to assist the NPRC government in fighting the RUF. Nigerian troops formed the backbone of the force and were critical in containing RUF advances near Freetown.

title: Executive Outcomes Mercenaries Deployed
description: The NPRC contracted the South African private military company Executive Outcomes in 1995 to push back RUF forces that had reached within 20 km of Freetown and seized the key Kono diamond fields. Within months Executive Outcomes recaptured the diamond mining areas and drove the RUF into remote regions, enabling elections.

title: Strasser Ousted; Bio Hands Over to Civilians
description: In January 1996, Brigadier Julius Maada Bio ousted Strasser in an intra-junta coup and pledged to hand power to a civilian government. Bio kept that promise: multi-party elections were held in February-March 1996 over RUF objections.

title: Kabbah Elected President
description: Ahmad Tejan Kabbah of the SLPP won the February–March 1996 presidential elections, defeating John Karefa-Smart in a second-round run-off. Kabbah's election was Sierra Leone's first competitive multi-party vote in more than two decades and raised hopes for an end to the civil war.

title: Abidjan Peace Accord
description: In November 1996, the Kabbah government and RUF signed the Abidjan Peace Accord, which included provisions for a ceasefire, transformation of the RUF into a political party, and departure of Executive Outcomes. The accord collapsed within months as the RUF failed to disarm.

title: AFRC Coup Ousts Kabbah
description: On 25 May 1997, the Armed Forces Revolutionary Council (AFRC) led by Major Johnny Paul Koroma overthrew President Kabbah and invited the RUF to join a joint junta government. Kabbah fled to Guinea and the international community widely condemned the coup.

title: UN Sanctions and Arms Embargo
description: The United Nations Security Council imposed sanctions on the AFRC/RUF junta in October 1997 through Resolution 1132, including an arms embargo and travel bans. ECOWAS also enforced a trade embargo designed to compel the junta's withdrawal.

title: ECOMOG Restores Kabbah
description: In February 1998, Nigerian-led ECOMOG forces launched a military offensive that drove the AFRC/RUF junta from Freetown and restored President Kabbah to power. Hundreds of junta members were subsequently tried; several were executed for treason.

title: RUF January Offensive — Operation No Living Thing
description: In January 1999, the RUF and AFRC launched a devastating assault on Freetown known as 'Operation No Living Thing,' killing thousands of civilians, amputating limbs, and burning neighbourhoods. The attack was eventually repulsed by ECOMOG but caused massive displacement.

title: Lomé Peace Accord
description: The Lomé Peace Agreement was signed in July 1999 between the Kabbah government and the RUF, granting Foday Sankoh the vice-presidency and blanket amnesty to combatants. The controversial accord was brokered by ECOWAS and the international community but was widely criticised by human rights organisations.

title: UNAMSIL Peacekeeping Mission Established
description: UN Security Council Resolution 1270 created the United Nations Mission in Sierra Leone (UNAMSIL) in October 1999 to help implement the Lomé Accord, eventually deploying up to 17,500 troops — the largest UN peacekeeping mission at that time. UNAMSIL faced a severe credibility crisis in 2000 when 500 peacekeepers were taken hostage by the RUF.

title: RUF Hostage Crisis and British Intervention
description: In May 2000, the RUF detained approximately 500 UNAMSIL peacekeepers as hostages and Freetown appeared at risk of falling again. Britain deployed around 1,000 troops in Operation Palliser, stabilising the situation, rescuing hostages, and providing the military backbone that eventually broke RUF power.

title: Foday Sankoh Arrested
description: RUF leader Foday Sankoh was captured by Sierra Leonean forces in May 2000 after a demonstration outside his Freetown residence turned violent and left dozens dead. His arrest effectively decapitated the RUF's political leadership and accelerated the collapse of the insurgency.

title: Disarmament Process Completed
description: The formal Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration (DDR) process was declared complete in January 2002, with over 70,000 fighters, including thousands of child soldiers, processed through UNAMSIL-supervised cantonment sites. The completion of DDR was a prerequisite for declaring the war officially over.

title: Civil War Officially Ends
description: President Kabbah formally declared the Sierra Leone civil war over on 18 January 2002 at a ceremony in Freetown attended by regional and international dignitaries. The eleven-year conflict had killed an estimated 50,000–70,000 people, displaced over two million, and left the country among the world's poorest.

title: Kabbah Re-elected; SLPP Wins Landslide
description: Ahmad Tejan Kabbah was re-elected president in May 2002 with 70 per cent of the vote in an election that also gave the SLPP a majority in parliament. The RUF received less than one per cent of the vote, a humiliating rejection by the electorate.

title: Special Court for Sierra Leone Established
description: The Special Court for Sierra Leone was established in January 2002 through an agreement between the United Nations and the Sierra Leonean government to try those bearing greatest responsibility for serious violations of international humanitarian law during the civil war. The court was innovative as a hybrid tribunal with both international and domestic law components.

title: Special Court Indictments and First Trials
description: By 2004, the Special Court for Sierra Leone had indicted thirteen individuals, including RUF leader Foday Sankoh (who died in custody in 2003), AFRC leader Johnny Paul Koroma (still at large), and former Civil Defence Forces commander Hinga Norman. The trials were seen as a landmark in post-conflict accountability in Africa.

title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission Report
description: The Sierra Leone Truth and Reconciliation Commission published its final report in 2004–2005, documenting systematic human rights abuses including amputations, sexual violence, and the use of child soldiers during the civil war. The report recommended reparations for survivors and reforms to prevent future conflicts.

title: Koroma and APC Win Landmark Election
description: Ernest Bai Koroma of the All People's Congress defeated the SLPP's Solomon Berewa in a second-round run-off in September 2007, marking the first peaceful transfer of power between parties since independence. International observers certified the election as largely free and fair.

title: Freetown Post-Election Violence
description: Violent clashes between APC and SLPP supporters in Freetown in early 2009 left several dead and hundreds displaced following the 2007 elections. The unrest underscored persistent ethnic and regional political polarisation and led to an ECOWAS-mediated dialogue.

title: Charles Taylor Trial Resumes at Special Court
description: The war crimes trial of former Liberian president Charles Taylor at the Special Court for Sierra Leone — relocated to The Hague — entered its defence phase in 2010. Taylor was charged with aiding and abetting RUF atrocities in exchange for conflict diamonds, making it the first international prosecution of a sitting African head of state.

title: Charles Taylor Convicted
description: Charles Taylor was found guilty by the Special Court for Sierra Leone in April 2012 on all eleven counts of war crimes and crimes against humanity, including terror, murder, rape, and use of child soldiers. He was sentenced to 50 years in prison — a watershed moment for international criminal justice and accountability for conflict diamonds.

title: Koroma Re-elected; Iron Ore Boom Begins
description: President Koroma won a second term in November 2012 elections considered broadly credible by observers. Sierra Leone simultaneously experienced a rapid iron ore export boom, with African Minerals' Tonkolili mine producing its first exports, briefly transforming GDP growth figures to among the highest in the world.

title: London Mining and African Minerals Iron Ore Exports Peak
description: Sierra Leone's iron ore sector expanded dramatically in 2013 as both London Mining's Marampa and African Minerals' Tonkolili mines reached near-full production capacity. The sector accounted for the majority of export revenues but remained structurally an enclave with limited linkage to the domestic economy.

title: Ebola Outbreak Begins
description: Sierra Leone confirmed its first Ebola cases in May 2014 in the Kailahun District following the spread of an outbreak originating in Guinea. The epidemic expanded rapidly, with the country eventually recording approximately 14,000 confirmed cases — the highest in the world — and around 4,000 deaths.

title: State of Emergency and International Ebola Response
description: President Koroma declared a state of emergency in July 2014 as Ebola cases surged, imposing quarantine zones and deploying the military. The international response escalated markedly after the UN Security Council declared Ebola a threat to international peace, with UK military medical units, US forces, and WHO teams providing critical support.

title: Iron Ore Sector Collapse
description: Global iron ore prices collapsed in 2014, devastating Sierra Leone's nascent mining sector. London Mining entered administration in October 2014, partly attributing the collapse to the Ebola crisis compounding already-falling commodity prices. African Minerals followed into administration in early 2015, effectively ending the iron ore boom.

title: Ebola Declared Eliminated
description: The World Health Organization declared Sierra Leone free of Ebola transmission on 7 November 2015, with a 42-day period having elapsed since the last confirmed case. The epidemic had killed an estimated 3,955 Sierra Leoneans, devastated the health system, and contracted GDP significantly.

title: Ebola Economic Contraction and Recovery Plan
description: Sierra Leone's economy contracted by approximately 21 per cent in 2015 as the twin shocks of the Ebola epidemic and iron ore price collapse combined. The government and donors launched a recovery plan supported by IMF and World Bank emergency financing, targeting health system rebuilding and economic diversification.

title: Mudslide Disaster Kills Hundreds
description: A catastrophic mudslide struck the Regent area near Freetown on 14 August 2017 following intense rainfall, killing over 500 people and displacing thousands. The disaster highlighted the acute vulnerability of informal hillside settlements in the capital and inadequate land-use regulation.

title: Julius Maada Bio Elected President
description: Julius Maada Bio of the SLPP defeated the APC's Samura Kamara in a run-off election in March 2018, returning the SLPP to power for the first time since 2007. Bio, who had briefly led the 1996 NPRC junta before handing over to civilians, campaigned on a human capital development agenda.

title: Free Quality Education Programme Launched
description: President Bio launched the Free Quality School Education programme in September 2018, making tuition-free education available from primary through senior secondary school. The flagship policy led to a surge in enrolment but also strained infrastructure and teacher supply.

title: Gender-Based Violence State of Emergency
description: President Bio declared a national state of emergency on gender-based violence in February 2019 after a series of high-profile rape cases, including the gang rape of a five-year-old. The declaration led to a dedicated Sexual Offences Model Court and drew international attention to endemic sexual violence.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Response
description: Sierra Leone confirmed its first COVID-19 cases in late March 2020 and quickly imposed lockdowns, drawing on institutional memory from the Ebola response. The pandemic disrupted the economy, particularly the informal sector, and depressed remittance inflows from the diaspora.

title: Diamond Revenue Dispute with Octea Mining
description: The Sierra Leonean government pursued Octea Mining, operator of the Koidu kimberlite diamond mine, over unpaid taxes and royalties amounting to hundreds of millions of dollars. The protracted dispute highlighted longstanding concerns about transfer pricing, illicit mineral flows, and weak state capacity to capture resource rents.

title: August Protests and Fuel Price Unrest
description: Large anti-government protests erupted in Freetown and other cities in August 2022, triggered by rising fuel and food prices aggravated by the global inflation shock following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. At least six people were killed in clashes with security forces, representing the worst civil unrest in years.

title: Food and Cost-of-Living Crisis
description: Sierra Leone entered a severe food and cost-of-living crisis in 2022, with inflation exceeding 40 per cent and the leone losing significant value. Declining foreign exchange reserves, disrupted rice and fuel imports, and stagnant wages pushed millions into food insecurity, with the UN warning of acute malnutrition in parts of the country.

title: Currency Depreciation and IMF Engagement
description: The Sierra Leonean leone depreciated sharply against the US dollar in 2022, prompting the government to redenominate the currency at a ratio of 1,000 old leones to 1 new leone in July 2022. The government simultaneously engaged the IMF for emergency balance-of-payments support.

title: Bio Re-elected Amid Disputed Results
description: President Julius Maada Bio was declared the winner of the June 2023 presidential election, narrowly avoiding a run-off according to official results. The main opposition APC party and several international observer missions raised serious concerns about the credibility of the vote tallying and result transmission process.

title: Post-Election APC Boycott and Political Crisis
description: Following the disputed 2023 election, the APC announced a boycott of all government institutions and parliamentary proceedings. The political standoff deepened ethnic and regional polarisation between the Mende-dominated south and Temne-dominated north, raising fears of renewed instability.

title: Attempted Military Mutiny — Aboo Bashar Incident
description: In November 2023, elements of the Sierra Leone Armed Forces attempted an armed takeover in Freetown, with attackers breaching the Wilberforce Barracks armoury and freeing prisoners from Pademba Road Prison. The government attributed the incident to a group led by former RSLAF officer Alhaji Bashar and declared it quickly suppressed, though its full scope remained disputed.

title: National Dialogue Commission Established
description: Under pressure from ECOWAS mediators, the Bio government and the APC agreed in late 2023 to establish a National Dialogue Commission to resolve the post-election crisis. The talks were facilitated by former Nigerian president Goodluck Jonathan and aimed at restoring opposition participation in governance.

title: Humanitarian Aid Dependency and Debt Concerns
description: Sierra Leone remained among the lowest-ranked countries on the Human Development Index in 2024, with significant portions of the national budget dependent on external donor support. The country faced growing concerns over debt sustainability as concessional financing conditions tightened in the post-COVID global environment.

title: Continued Iron Ore and Diamond Export Disputes
description: Sierra Leone continued to grapple with revenue leakage from its extractive sector in 2024, with parliamentary debates over renegotiating mining contracts with Chinese and Western companies operating iron ore and diamond concessions. Civil society organisations documented large gaps between declared export values and independently estimated ore grades.
